entries.snippet: Kinshasa accuses its neighbour of committing various violations since the 1994 Rwanda genocide.

entries.title: Just how much trouble is Canada's economy in?

entries.title: Trump nominates former Oklahoma state trooper to head ICE
entries.snippet: President Trump nominated Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to direct Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The agency hasn't had a Senate-confirmed director since the Obama administration.

entries.title: Critical fire weather complicates firefighting efforts in massive Utah wildfire
entries.snippet: Firefighters working on the nation's largest current wildfire, burning in southern Utah, are being challenged by historic weather conditions. Extreme wildfire behavior is expected to continue through the weekend.

entries.title: Uzbekistan makes its World Cup debut, a first for Central Asia
entries.snippet: The country is the first Central Asian nation to qualify for the World Cup, and Uzbek fans have reveled in showcasing their country and culture. The country's president calls the team a symbol of the "new Uzbekistan."

entries.title: Opinion: Ranch dressing is a winner at the World Cup games
entries.snippet: NPR's Scott Simon reflects on the popularity of ranch dressing among international visitors to the U.S. during the World Cup games.

entries.title: Trump administration partially lifts export ban on Anthropic's most advanced AI model
entries.snippet: The U.S. government is asserting a new level of influence over AI, controlling which companies can access Anthropic's new models. OpenAI agreed to let the administration screen users of its new model.

entries.title: If a Lyme disease vaccine gets approved, how would it go over? We asked hunters
entries.snippet: Drugmakers are working on a potential new shot to prevent the tick-borne illness. How might it fare in the era of vaccine skepticism?

entries.title: As Supreme Court expands Trump's immigration power, experts warn of steeper U.S. population decline
entries.snippet: The U.S. population was already aging and tilting toward decline. After the Supreme Court confirmed Trump's power to deport hundreds of thousands of foreign migrants, population decline could accelerate.

entries.title: How coach Mauricio Pochettino made believers out of the U.S. World Cup team
entries.snippet: Pochettino was the biggest name the U.S. men's soccer team had ever hired. His rebuild was bumpy at times — but now, with the U.S. headed to the World Cup knockout stage, the players are all in.

entries.title: Inside a secretive Ukrainian team launching deep drone strikes at Russia
entries.snippet: Ukraine's long-range drones are striking deep inside Russia, up to 1,200 miles away, hitting oil refineries and depots. NPR recently spent time with one of the Ukrainian strike teams launching drones at Russian targets.

entries.title: This mindset shift can help you get better at using up your leftovers
entries.snippet: Don't let your leftovers go to waste. Cookbook authors share clever storage techniques — like an "Eat Me First" box in your fridge — and cooking tricks to help you make the most of your food scraps.

entries.title: Man with same name as U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan is eligible for Alaska's primary ballot, judge rules
entries.snippet: The judge ruled that the division's decision to exclude Dan J. Sullivan because his candidacy was not "in good faith" was not based on the Constitution, Alaska law or the division's own regulations.

entries.title: Trump-backed Julia Letlow faces John Fleming in Louisiana GOP Senate runoff
entries.snippet: U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow, who was endorsed by Trump, and state Treasurer John Fleming are competing in the runoff. The two finished ahead of Sen. Bill Cassidy in the May 16 primary after Trump denounced the two-term senator, who voted to convict him following his 2021 impeachment.

entries.title: Trump says he is nominating former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer as ICE director
entries.snippet: Schroyer's nomination comes after former ICE director Todd Lyons resigned at the end of May. David Venturella, a former executive at a private prison operator, has been serving as the acting head of the agency.

entries.title: Desperation mounts in Venezuela as the earthquake death toll rises to 1,430
entries.snippet: Venezuela's government said families reported at least 68,900 people missing, three days after the one-two punch of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes devastated the South American nation.

entries.title: World Cup final day of group play will set the field for the round of 32
entries.snippet: Going into the final day of group play at the World Cup, there are essentially eight teams vying for four spots in the round of 32.

entries.title: U.S. military says it struck multiple targets in Iran as ceasefire is strained by 2nd day of attacks
entries.snippet: The ongoing strikes in the Persian Gulf show the danger of the Iran war again spinning out of control, even after Iran and the U.S. reached an interim deal to try and agree on a final accord to end the conflict.

entries.title: Lebanon's deal with Israel requires Hezbollah to disarm. That might be difficult
entries.snippet: Lebanon and Israel signed the deal in Washington on Friday without Hezbollah. The agreement links Israel's withdrawal from Lebanon to the Iran-backed militant group's disarmament, something Hezbollah rejects.

entries.title: Tens of thousands march in the first Budapest Pride since Viktor Orbán was voted out
entries.snippet: Saturday's Pride march came a little more than a year after Orbán's nationalist-populist government passed legislation and a constitutional amendment to outlaw the event, drawing criticism from human rights groups and politicians across the European Union.

entries.title: At the Great American State Fair, you can find a dinosaur's rib cage. Unity is another matter
entries.snippet: The fair kicked off this week and is a run by Freedom 250, an organization created by President Donald Trump to run his administration's official events.

entries.title: Andy Burnham distanced himself from UK Prime Minister Starmer, but may be stuck with his policies
entries.snippet: Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester who was sworn into Parliament hours after Starmer announced his resignation on Monday, will be constrained by the platform the center-left Labour Party was elected on that decisively ended 14 years of Conservative rule in 2024.

entries.title: Residents on notice as fast-moving fire in Utah, the largest in the U.S., blackens more forestland
entries.snippet: Firefighters are facing more challenges on the ground from what fire managers and experts call unprecedented conditions.

entries.title: Apple increases prices for Macs and iPads, blaming memory chip shortage fueled by AI
entries.snippet: The Cupertino, California-based company called the demand spike an "unprecedented challenge" for the consumer electronics industry.

entries.title: Americans are inundated with suspected scams. New polls show why few victims report them
entries.snippet: Most Americans are inundated with scam attempts on a daily basis — and about 3 in 10 have personally lost money or personal information to scams, according to a new AP-NORC survey.

entries.title: DNC plans weekend of local events to focus on affordability concerns under Trump
entries.snippet: Two years ago, Democrats were the ones accused of being indifferent to Americans' anger about rising prices. Now they're pointing the finger at Trump, who has downplayed the impact of lingering inflation.

entries.snippet: The WNBA has suspended Phoenix's Alyssa Thomas for one game after she made contact with her fist to Caitlin Clark's throat in Wednesday night's matchup against Indiana.

entries.snippet: On Friday, the U.S. military conducted new strikes against Iran in response to what President Trump said was Tehran's violation of the ceasefire. Nick Schifirin reports.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Venezuela earthquakes: Nearly 7 million may be impacted — UN
entries.snippet: The projection includes up to two million people in the capital, Caracas. Rescue teams are racing against time to save survivors, three days after the twin quakes that killed 1,430 people. DW has more.

entries.title: Ukraine strikes Russian weapons plant, Moscow fuel hub
entries.snippet: The two attacks, in Volgograd and Vladimir regions, are part of President Zelenskyy's strategy to bring the war to the Russian people and force Putin into peace negotiations.

entries.title: Why is the US targeting Germany's drug industry?
entries.snippet: A new trade probe is reigniting a long-running clash over who should pay for medical innovation. Washington argues Germans benefit from lower prices while US patients shoulder a disproportionate share of the costs.

entries.title: Germany news: Heat record broken for second consecutive day
entries.snippet: As Europe's heatwave rages, Germany breaks all-time temperature record for the second day in a row. Elsewhere, politicians bicker over reforms and industry blames train operator DB for billions in losses.

entries.title: Rome celebrates 80 years of Italy's iconic Vespa scooter
entries.snippet: Thousands of Vespa riders took to Rome's streets to mark Vespa's 80th birthday. The wasp-waisted scooter became a symbol of Italy's rebirth after World War II.

entries.title: The 'Flamingo Revolution': What's behind Albania's protests?
entries.snippet: For weeks now, images of crowds of Albanians protesting on the streets have been relayed around the world. The protesters say they are fighting for democracy. PM Edi Rama insists the movement is part of a hybrid war.

entries.title: US allows partial release of Anthropic's Mythos AI model
entries.snippet: Only a small group of American firms will get access to Anthropic's AI Model Mythos 5, however, it is unclear which companies will be selected.

entries.title: Why is Germany taking a big stake in a major tankmaker?
entries.snippet: The German government will buy a 40% stake in tankmaker KNDS. The deal is as much about control in the critical defense sector as it is about the Franco-German relationship.

entries.title: Why Germany's Deutsche Bahn will face delays for many years
entries.snippet: Delayed, unreliable and forced into long detours due to construction: Germany no longer sets the pace when it comes to rail travel — and this is unlikely to change anytime soon. The company is mired in a deep crisis.

entries.title: Military-age Ukrainian men could lose EU protection
entries.snippet: The European Commission has suggested withdrawing protection status for military-age Ukrainian males. A number of EU countries support the move — and so does Kyiv.

entries.title: Europe faces scorching weekend as heat wave moves east
entries.snippet: Europe's heat wave is expected to move east after causing record temperatures in several countries. But Germany still has a couple of torrid days ahead. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Balochistan activist's life sentence raises fear of unrest
entries.snippet: With the conviction of a leading rights campaigner, Pakistan has drawn criticism from rights groups and sparked fears it could deepen unrest in Balochistan and weaken trust in peaceful activism.

entries.title: India news: PM Modi embarks on two-day Seychelles visit
entries.snippet: India's PM Narendra Modi is set to be the Guest of Honor at the Golden Jubilee of Seychelles' National Day. His visit is also aimed at stregnthening martime, security and economic cooperation. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Comedy legend Mel Brooks turns 100
entries.snippet: A parody of Adolf Hitler in the landmark 1968 movie "The Producers" was just the beginning for US actor Mel Brooks. The 100-year-old comedian is still on a roll today.

entries.title: Court upholds Weinstein rape conviction
entries.snippet: A California court has upheld the conviction of disgraced movie mogul Harvey Weinstein but said a lower court judge must resentence him. Allegations against Weinstein sparked the #MeToo movement.

entries.title: US carries out 'additional strikes' on Iran
entries.snippet: The US military said "additional strikes" have been carried out on targets in Iran. CENTCOM said the strikes were in response to a drone strike on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. DW has more.

entries.title: Trump foe John Bolton pleads guilty in classified docs case
entries.snippet: Bolton faces as many as five years in prison. He had earlier served as Trump's national security adviser during the president's first term in office, but later resigned over his differences with Trump.

entries.title: US, Lebanon, Israel sign framework agreement
entries.snippet: US Secretary ‌of ⁠State ⁠Marco ​Rubio has announced ​a trilateral ​framework ‌agreement. Lebanese officials began direct talks with Israel in Washington in April.

entries.title: Creative climate messaging and other eco wins of the week
entries.snippet: An artist in Mali and climate scientists in the US are finding new ways to inform the public about the climate crisis.
